name: ig-islamic-dilemma-study
caption:
A free 16-session reading club for The Islamic Dilemma by Christopher W. Frost (@SCApologia) — and the first thing to say is: buy his book.

You need it to do the club, and it earns the money. Frost doesn't argue from Christian premises — he works through the Qur'an's own text, and his footnotes send you out to mainstream Islamic-studies scholarship rather than leaving you holding a slogan. If you have ever wanted one careful book on this question, that is the one to get.

The argument, in short. The Qur'an speaks warmly of the Torah and the Gospel — calling them revelation from God, "guidance and light," and telling Jews and Christians to follow them. Yet it also contradicts them on central points, from the crucifixion of Jesus to the fatherhood of God. Frost lays that tension out and asks what it means.

Chris has seen this study and approved it — and we want to be clear about what is whose: the summaries, questions and judgements in it are ours, not his, and nothing in it reproduces his text.

So get the book, then work through the club with a friend or a small group. Every session has discussion questions, and the optional Apologia Daily deep-dives are clearly marked as ours and entirely skippable.

The aim is not to win an argument. It is to lay the tension out honestly, and to talk it over kindly (1 Peter 3:15).

The club is free — link in bio. The book is his, and worth it.

sub.t: The Islamic Dilemma — published with his approval.
